decisionsTitle: The paper confirmation says what it is for, what it does and what the person receives
decisionsSection:
**The owner, 2026-10-02**, on a registration still waiting for its email confirmation (a club member he wants at the start), after reading the «Ziua cursei» box: «Dacă fac „confirmare pe hârtie” primește mail de declarația și așa?» And, once told: «Pune tooltip și info in back-office pt asta».

### What the caption said, and what it left unsaid

The box's caption (`desk.fastTrackHelp`) read: «Înscrierea e confirmată pe loc, fără email; participantul semnează declarația pe hârtie, iar tu o înregistrezi. Dacă e plin, intră pe lista de așteptare.» It left four facts out, and its «fără email» read as if the person got none:

- **When.** The press is for the race-day desk, with the declaration the participant signed on paper in front of the staff member. The staff member records it on their own name — the declaration (`method = PAPER`, `attested_by_staff_user_id`) and, only on a registration still waiting for its address, the address too (`email_confirmed_by_staff_user_id`). Nobody on staff signs for anybody (§67, `AGENTS.md` §15.11).
- **The place — and which rows it concerns.** `confirmByStaff` goes through the allocator under the event lock (§67, §348, §615) only for a registration that has no place yet (waiting for its address, or a lapsed hold): it joins the waiting list when the event is full or somebody waits, and a full waiting list refuses the press, rolling the transaction back. A registration that already holds its place (`PENDING_DECLARATION`, `WAITLIST_OFFERED`) goes straight to `acceptDeclarationOnPaper`: no allocator, no waiting list, because the hold already occupies the place.
- **The email — and only with a place.** When the person gets the place, `acceptDeclarationOnPaper` queues `REGISTRATION_CONFIRMED` (the QR code, the race number, the declaration's copy as after an electronic signature, §95) and the club's copy and notice. No «complete the declaration» email is sent: there is nothing left to sign. When the press puts the person on the waiting list, `confirmByStaff` returns before that: no declaration is recorded, no confirmation email goes, and the person signs later, when offered a place.
- **What it is not.** It is the desk's verb for a person standing there, not a way to skip the email confirmation before the race. For an address that never got its email, the Administrator's «Retrimite emailul» is the verb.

### The new words

Four catalogue lines (`Admin.desk.paperWhen`, `paperPlace`, `paperEmail`, `paperNot`, each under 200 characters, in both languages, quoting only labels the backoffice shows). Each says «who is concerned» where it is not everybody: the address clause is «if the address was not confirmed», the place line starts «someone without a place yet», the email line starts «if they get the place» and says that on the waiting list nothing is recorded. The review of the first version found these stated without condition (a false promise of the email on a full event; the allocator's rule read on a row whose own hold fills the race).

- **The registration's page, «Ziua cursei».** An «i» beside the box's title (`ui/PaperConfirmationTip`, the four lines one under another, the tooltip's newline of §257) and, under the button, a caption of three of the four lines — when, what the person receives if they get the place, what it is not (about 500 characters; the owner asked for tooltip and info, and the caption is the always-visible «info», the «i» the full text with the place's rule). The place line is in the «i» only: the press itself answers it with the refusal's sentence. The «i» and the caption show only where the button does, on a registration that is not yet confirmed.
- **The registrations list's row menu.** «Confirmă pe hârtie» in the «⋮» menu carries the same four lines as its tooltip (`paperConfirmationText`, the one function `PaperConfirmationTip` uses, so the three places never drift), the way «Dă-i un loc» carries the refusal's sentence (§592). The item is offered there on a registration that already holds its place.
- **The confirm dialog** (`registrations.confirmOnPaperBody`, `…BodyMinor`): its words kept, one sentence added — «Apoi pleacă emailul de confirmare.» The dialog's generic line that an email will be sent already followed; this one says which.
- **The desk.** The same «i», once, beside `desk.rowHelp` — the page's always-visible line that says what the row buttons do and already names «Confirmă pe hârtie». Not on each row: twenty rows would be twenty identical «i» in a column the volunteer is scanning for names, and the help line is where the page already answers «ce face butonul ăsta». `DeskRow` is untouched. The volunteer reads the same four lines, and the last says that resending the email is the Administrator's.
- **The walk-in form's help** (`desk.fastTrackHelp`, the same fast track): the false-sounding «fără email» became «fără link din email»; the declaration is named («semnează declarația pe hârtie»); and the waiting list comes before the email — «dacă e plin, intră pe lista de așteptare; altfel primește emailul de confirmare».
- **The guide.** The desk's «Nu și-a semnat declarația» job gains the step about the email the person receives, in both languages.

### What was refused

A new verb, a new email or any bypass: the button, its dialog, the allocator and the audit are what they were, and the rule of `AGENTS.md` §15.11 stands — a staff member records what the participant signed; the press is not a way around the allocator, the declaration or the participant's own signature. Also refused: an «i» on every desk row (noise).

**Consequences.** `registrations/ui/PaperConfirmationTip.tsx` (new, with `paperConfirmationText`), the registration's page, the desk page, the registrations list's row menu, `messages/{ro,en}.json` (`Admin.desk.paper*`, `fastTrackHelp`, `Admin.registrations.confirmOnPaperBody*`, the guide's desk job). Test: `tests/integration/registrations/paper-confirmation-tip.test.ts` (both locales; the tip's four lines in order; the box's «i» and caption; one «i» on the desk however many rows; the list menu's tooltip); `tests/unit/i18n/plain-words.test.ts` and `tests/unit/staff/guide-words.test.ts` hold the words. No migration, no dependency, no behaviour change.
changelogLine: - **«Confirmă pe hârtie» says what it is for** — an «i» beside «Ziua cursei», once on the desk and as the tooltip of the list's row menu, a caption and a line in the confirm window: at the desk, with the paper the participant signed; a person without a place goes through the waiting list when full; with a place they get the confirmation email with the QR code; and it is not a shortcut around the email confirmation. §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Given a registration the desk's paper confirmation is offered on, when the staff member opens its page, the desk or the registrations list's row menu, then the registration page's «Ziua cursei» box carries an «i» beside its title and a caption, the desk carries one «i» beside the line that says what the row buttons do (never one per row), the list's «Confirmă pe hârtie» item carries the same text as its tooltip, the confirm window says the confirmation email follows, and the four lines say, in Romanian and English: that it is for the race-day desk with the declaration the participant signed on paper in front of staff, recorded on the staff member's name (the address too only if it was not confirmed); that a person without a place yet gets it through the allocator (the waiting list when full, a full list refuses); that if they get the place they receive the confirmation email with the QR code, the number and the declaration's copy and no declaration-to-sign email, and on the waiting list nothing is recorded; and that it is not a shortcut around the email confirmation before the race. No button, dialog, verb or allocator rule changed (2026-10-02, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).
